connectors.name: Azure DevOps
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from the work items a WIQL query returns.
connectors.auth: Signs in with your Azure identity — `az login` is usually all it needs.

triggers.label: Work item matches the query
triggers.description: Fires once per work item the WIQL query newly returns.

actions.label: Create a work item
actions.description: Add a work item to the board and return its id and url.

actions.label: Update a work item
actions.description: Change the title, state, description or assignee of a work item.

env.name: ADO_ORGANIZATION
env.description: Name or URL, e.g. "contoso" or https://dev.azure.com/contoso

env.name: ADO_QUERY
env.description: Work items to poll, e.g. SELECT [System.Id] FROM WorkItems WHERE [System.State] = 'New' ORDER BY [System.ChangedDate] DESC

env.name: ADO_TOP
env.description: Upper bound on work items read in one poll.

connectors.name: GitHub
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from GitHub issues and pull requests, and open, close or comment on them from a step.
connectors.auth: Borrows the GitHub CLI's login — `gh auth login` is all it needs, and no token is stored here.

triggers.label: An issue is created
triggers.description: Fires for each issue opened since the last poll.

triggers.label: A pull request is opened
triggers.description: Fires for each pull request opened since the last poll.

actions.label: Create an issue
actions.description: Open a new issue in the connected repository.

actions.label: Close an issue
actions.description: Close an issue or pull request in the connected repository.

actions.label: Comment on an issue
actions.description: Post a comment on an issue or pull request.

env.name: GITHUB_OWNER
env.description: User or organisation, e.g. vorn-run

env.name: GITHUB_REPO
env.description: Repository name on its own, without the owner

env.name: GITHUB_LABELS
env.description: Comma-separated. Applies to the issue trigger only.

connectors.name: GitLab
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from GitLab issues, merge requests and pipeline results, and create or comment on issues and merge requests from a step.
connectors.auth: Borrows the GitLab CLI's login — `glab auth login` is all it needs — or takes a personal access token if you would rather paste one.

triggers.label: An issue is created
triggers.description: Fires once for each issue created in the project since the last poll.

triggers.label: A merge request is opened
triggers.description: Fires once for each merge request opened in the project since the last poll.

triggers.label: A pipeline finishes
triggers.description: Fires once for each pipeline that reaches success, failed, canceled or skipped, with the status on the item.

actions.label: Create an issue
actions.description: Open a new issue in a project.

actions.label: Comment on an issue
actions.description: Post a note on an issue.

actions.label: Comment on a merge request
actions.description: Post a note on a merge request.

actions.label: Get a project
actions.description: Read a project by path or id.

actions.label: List open merge requests
actions.description: The open merge requests of a project, most recently updated first.

actions.label: Get an issue
actions.description: Read one issue by its number.

env.name: GITLAB_BASE_URL
env.description: Instance URL without a trailing slash. Leave the default for gitlab.com.

env.name: GITLAB_PROJECT
env.description: Path such as group/project, or the numeric id. The triggers poll this project.

env.name: GITLAB_TOKEN
env.description: Leave empty to borrow the glab CLI login. Needs scope api, or read_api for the triggers and read-only actions.

env.name: GITLAB_REF
env.description: Branch or tag whose pipelines to watch. Blank for every ref.

connectors.name: Azure Data Explorer
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from the rows a KQL query returns.
connectors.auth: Signs in with your Azure identity — `az login` is usually all it needs.

triggers.label: Query returns a row
triggers.description: Fires once per new row returned by the configured KQL query.

actions.label: Run a KQL query
actions.description: Run a read-only query and return its rows.

env.name: KUSTO_CLUSTER
env.description: Cluster name or URL, e.g. "help" or https://help.kusto.windows.net

env.name: KUSTO_QUERY
env.description: Query to poll. Reference vorn_since and vorn_limit to bound it.

env.name: KUSTO_ID_COLUMN
env.description: Column holding a stable per-row id. Vorn dedupes on it.

env.name: KUSTO_TIMESTAMP_COLUMN
env.description: Column the poll watermark advances from.

env.name: KUSTO_LOOKBACK
env.description: How far back the very first poll looks, e.g. 30m, 2h, 7d.

connectors.name: Linear
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from Linear issues, and comment or close them from a step.
connectors.auth: Uses a Linear personal API key, created at linear.app/settings/api.

triggers.label: An issue is created or changed
triggers.description: Fires for each issue the query returns that Vorn has not seen at this time.

actions.label: Comment on an issue
actions.description: Post a comment on a Linear issue.

actions.label: Create an issue
actions.description: Open a new Linear issue and return its identifier and url.

actions.label: Close an issue
actions.description: Move an issue to the first completed state its team defines.

env.name: LINEAR_API_KEY
env.description: Create a personal API key at linear.app/settings/api.

env.name: LINEAR_TEAM_KEY
env.description: Upper-case key such as ENG. Leave blank for every team you can see.

env.name: LINEAR_STATE_TYPE
env.description: One of backlog, unstarted, started, completed, canceled. Blank for all states.

connectors.name: Notion
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from Notion database pages, and create or update them.
connectors.auth: Paste a Notion integration token, then share the pages you want it to see with the connection in Notion. There is no Notion CLI to sign in with.

triggers.label: A page is created or changed
triggers.description: Fires once per page in the database that Vorn has not seen at this time. Deleted and moved pages produce no event — polling only sees what still matches.

actions.label: Create a page
actions.description: Add a page to the configured data source.

actions.label: Update a page
actions.description: Set properties on an existing page.

actions.label: Find pages
actions.description: Query the configured data source and return the pages it matches.

env.name: NOTION_TOKEN
env.description: An internal integration token or personal API key from notion.so/profile/integrations. There is no Notion CLI to sign in with.

env.name: NOTION_DATABASE_ID
env.description: Paste the database URL, or the 32-character id from it.

env.name: NOTION_DATA_SOURCE_ID
env.description: Only needed when the database has more than one data source. Blank resolves it.

env.name: NOTION_FILTER
env.description: A JSON filter in Notion's own syntax, ANDed with the poll watermark.

env.name: NOTION_STATUS_PROPERTY
env.description: Name of the property carrying status. Blank uses the first status, then select, property.

connectors.name: PostgreSQL
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from new rows in a PostgreSQL database, and query or write to it from a step.
connectors.auth: Paste the database's connection string (postgres://user:password@host:5432/db?sslmode=require) from your provider's dashboard or your DBA; a read-only role is enough for triggers.

triggers.label: New rows in a table
triggers.description: Fires once per row inserted after the last seen value of the ordering column.

triggers.label: Rows matching a query
triggers.description: Fires once per row your SELECT returns beyond the cursor value it was last run with.

actions.label: Run a query
actions.description: Run SQL text with positional parameters and return its rows and row count.

actions.label: Select rows
actions.description: Read rows from a table, with an optional parameterised WHERE.

actions.label: Insert a row
actions.description: Insert one row and return it as stored.

actions.label: Update rows
actions.description: Set columns on the rows a WHERE matches and return how many changed.

actions.label: List tables
actions.description: List the tables and views in a schema that the role can see.

actions.label: Describe a table
actions.description: List the columns of a table with their types and nullability.

env.name: DATABASE_URL
env.description: libpq URI: postgres://user:password@host:5432/database?sslmode=require. Your provider shows it on the database page; otherwise ask your DBA. A read-only role is enough for triggers.

env.name: PG_TABLE
env.description: For "new rows": table or schema.table to watch.

env.name: PG_ORDERING_COLUMN
env.description: For "new rows": a column that only grows, such as id or created_at.

env.name: PG_KEY_COLUMN
env.description: The column that identifies a row, usually the primary key. Defaults to the ordering column for "new rows"; required for "rows matching a query".

env.name: PG_QUERY
env.description: For "rows matching a query": a SELECT with $1 where the cursor goes and, optionally, $2 for the limit, ordered by the cursor column ascending.

env.name: PG_CURSOR_COLUMN
env.description: For "rows matching a query": the result column the cursor advances from.

env.name: PG_START_FROM
env.description: Value of the ordering or cursor column to start after. Required for "rows matching a query"; for "new rows", blank means the newest page.

env.name: PG_TITLE_COLUMN
env.description: Column to use as the item title. Blank uses the table and key.

connectors.name: Slack
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from Slack messages, thread replies and channel members, and post, reply or react from a step.
connectors.auth: Uses a bot token from a Slack app installed to the workspace: api.slack.com/apps, OAuth & Permissions, Bot User OAuth Token.

triggers.label: A message is posted in a channel
triggers.description: Fires for each new message in the configured channel. Bot and system messages are skipped unless includeBots is true.

triggers.label: A reply is posted in a thread
triggers.description: Fires for each new reply under the configured parent message.

triggers.label: A member joins a channel
triggers.description: Fires once for each user id in the channel that has not been seen before.

actions.label: Post a message
actions.description: Post a message to a channel, optionally under a thread or with Block Kit blocks.

actions.label: Reply in a thread
actions.description: Post a reply under a parent message.

actions.label: Add a reaction
actions.description: React to a message with an emoji.

actions.label: List channels
actions.description: List the public and private channels the bot can see, unarchived only.

actions.label: Get a channel
actions.description: Read one channel by id.

actions.label: Find a user by email
actions.description: Look a user up by the address registered on the workspace.

actions.label: Get a user
actions.description: Read one user by id.

env.name: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
env.description: Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…) of a Slack app installed to the workspace, from api.slack.com/apps under OAuth & Permissions.

env.name: SLACK_CHANNEL
env.description: Channel id such as C0123456789 the triggers watch. The bot must be a member.

env.name: SLACK_THREAD_TS
env.description: The parent message ts, such as 1512085950.000216, for the reply trigger.

env.name: SLACK_INCLUDE_BOTS
env.description: true delivers messages with a subtype or a bot_id too; joins, topic changes, app posts.

env.name: SLACK_LIMIT
env.description: Messages read per request, 1 to 999.

connectors.name: Telegram
connectors.description: Trigger workflows from Telegram messages, and send, reply or edit from a step.
connectors.auth: Paste a bot token from @BotFather. There is no Telegram CLI to sign in with, and Telegram's OAuth grants only outbound messaging, never reads.

triggers.label: A message arrives
triggers.description: Fires for each new or edited message the bot can see. Telegram deletes unread updates after 24 hours and has no history endpoint, so this sees nothing sent before the connection was made.

actions.label: Send a message
actions.description: Post a message to a chat the bot is in.

actions.label: Reply to a message
actions.description: Post a message as a reply, so it threads under the original.

actions.label: Edit a message
actions.description: Replace the text of a message this bot sent.

env.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
env.description: Create a bot with @BotFather in Telegram and paste the token it gives you. One token can only be read by one connection — a second one steals this one’s messages.

env.name: TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID
env.description: Numeric chat id, or @username for a public channel. Blank watches every chat the bot is in.

env.name: TELEGRAM_UPDATE_TYPES
env.description: Comma-separated. One or more of message, edited_message, channel_post, edited_channel_post.

env.name: TELEGRAM_POLL_TIMEOUT
env.description: How long Telegram may hold the connection open waiting for a message. 0 is short polling, which Telegram documents as being for testing only.

env.name: TELEGRAM_LIMIT
env.description: 1 to 100. Anything left over is read by the next poll.

templates.name: Morning digest
templates.description: Every weekday morning, gather what changed overnight and have an agent write it up.

config.prompt:
Write a short digest of these commits for the team:

{{steps.execute-script.output}}

templates.name: Triage new tasks
templates.description: When a task is created, have an agent read it and say what it will take.

templates.name: Webhook to report
templates.description: Take a request from another system, look at what it says, and post the ones that matter on somewhere else.
